name: Tennis
summary: Tennis is a net sport in which one or two players a side use stringed rackets to hit a felt-covered ball over a net and into the opposing half of a rectangular court. It is played on grass, clay, hard and indoor courts at clubs, parks and schools around the world, and its rules are set by the International Tennis Federation.

origin.text: Modern lawn tennis took shape in England in the 1870s
origin.editorNote: LTA dates Major Walter Clopton Wingfield's introduction of lawn tennis to 1873; the AELTC and the first Wimbledon Championships followed in 1877

formats.name: Singles
formats.description: One player a side, using the singles sidelines.

formats.name: Doubles
formats.description: Two players a side, using the full width of the court.

formats.name: Mixed doubles
formats.description: A man and a woman on each side.

relatedSports.note: The indoor game tennis grew out of.

name: Pickleball
summary: Pickleball is a net sport played with solid paddles and a light, perforated plastic ball on a court the size of a doubles badminton court, with a lowered net. Serves are underhand and a non-volley zone next to the net ("the kitchen") stops players volleying close in. It began in the United States and is now played in parks, sports halls and dedicated clubs worldwide.

origin.text: Invented in 1965 on Bainbridge Island, Washington, USA
origin.editorNote: USA Pickleball credits Joel Pritchard, Bill Bell and Barney McCallum
origin.citation: What is Pickleball?: History of Pickleball

name: Squash
summary: Squash is an indoor racket sport in which two players share a four-walled court and take turns to hit a small, hollow rubber ball against the front wall above a metal strip called the tin. The ball may come off the side and back walls, and rallies are won when the opponent cannot return it before it bounces twice. It is played in clubs, gyms and universities in over a hundred countries.

origin.text: Developed at Harrow School, England, in the 19th century as an offshoot of rackets
origin.editorNote: WSF history places the start at Harrow School in the mid-19th century, combining racquets and fives; its court specification says around 1830

formats.name: Doubles
formats.description: Played on a wider doubles court in international competition.

name: Badminton
summary: Badminton is a net sport in which players use light rackets to hit a feathered or synthetic shuttlecock over a high net, scoring when it lands in the opposing court or the opponent fails to return it. It is played indoors almost everywhere at competitive level, with singles and doubles, and is especially strong in Asia and northern Europe.

origin.text: The modern game was codified in England in the 19th century and takes its name from Badminton House, Gloucestershire
origin.editorNote: BWF corporate site and Badminton England history page could not be read on 2026-10-24 (403 / script-rendered); Olympics.com blocked. Commonly linked to Badminton House, Gloucestershire

relatedSports.relation: Shares the name, uses a ball

name: Table tennis
summary: Table tennis is played on a table divided by a low net, with players using small rubber-faced bats to hit a 40 mm plastic ball so that it bounces once on the opponent's half. Rallies are fast and spin-heavy. It is played in clubs, schools and homes worldwide and has been an Olympic sport since 1988.

origin.text: Began in England in the late 19th century as an after-dinner parlour game, often called ping-pong
origin.editorNote: ITTF site returned 403 on 2026-10-24; Table Tennis England history page covers the association (Ping Pong Association, 1921 revival), not the game's origin

formats.name: Doubles
formats.description: Partners must hit the ball alternately.

name: Racquetball
summary: Racquetball is a fast indoor sport played with short-handled rackets and a bouncy hollow rubber ball in a fully enclosed court, where every wall and the ceiling are in play. The ball must reach the front wall before touching the floor. It is most popular in the Americas and is governed internationally by the International Racquetball Federation.

origin.text: Created in the United States around 1950 by Joe Sobek, who called it paddle rackets
origin.editorNote: Corrected from "Created around 1950 in Greenwich, Connecticut, USA" on 2026-10-24; USA Racquetball names Sobek and 1950 but not Greenwich

formats.name: Cut-throat
formats.description: Three players, each serving player against the other two.

relatedSports.relation: British cousin on a squash court

name: Platform tennis
summary: Platform tennis is an outdoor winter doubles game played with perforated paddles and a sponge-rubber ball on a small raised deck surrounded by tight wire screens, which stay in play after the ball bounces. The deck is often heated so snow and ice can be cleared. It is played mainly in the north-eastern United States.

origin.text: Devised in 1928 in Scarsdale, New York, USA
origin.editorNote: APTA: started in 1928 in Scarsdale by neighbours looking for a winter racquet sport; it does not name Blanchard and Cogswell
origin.citation: What is Platform Tennis?: Platform Tennis Origins

name: Soft tennis
summary: Soft tennis is a form of tennis played with a soft, inflated rubber ball and lighter rackets on a standard-size tennis court. The softer ball favours long rallies and makes doubles the main format. It is played widely in Japan, Korea and Taiwan.

origin.text: Began in Japan in 1884, adapting lawn tennis to softer rubber balls
origin.editorNote: Corrected from "Developed in Japan in the 1880s, when imported tennis balls were scarce" on 2026-10-24; the ISTF does not mention scarce tennis balls

name: Crossminton
summary: Crossminton is a fast shuttle sport with no net: two players stand in square fields set some distance apart and hit a heavier, faster shuttle (a "speeder") back and forth with small rackets. It can be played on grass, beaches, hard courts or indoors, including at night with illuminated shuttles.

origin.text: Developed in Berlin, Germany, around 2000 by Bill Brandes, and first marketed as Speedminton
origin.editorNote: Corrected from "Developed in Germany around 2001, first marketed as Speedminton" on 2026-10-24. Speedminton GmbH took the idea over in 2003; the sport was called speed badminton, then crossminton from 2016

name: Beach tennis
summary: Beach tennis is played on sand with solid paddles and a low-pressure ball, which must be hit before it touches the ground, over a high net on a court the size of a beach volleyball court. Doubles is the standard format. It began in Italy and is now played on beaches and sand courts in Europe and the Americas, with ITF-sanctioned events.

origin.text: Began on the beaches around Ravenna, Italy, in the late 20th century
origin.editorNote: ITF Rules of Beach Tennis 2023 and itftennis.com pages checked 2026-10-24: no origin given. Commonly linked to Ravenna, Italy

name: Paddle tennis
summary: Paddle tennis is a scaled-down form of tennis played with solid paddles and a depressurised tennis ball on a smaller court with an underhand serve. It is played mainly in the United States, notably in California, and the US association now promotes it as POP Tennis.

origin.text: Devised in New York in the late 1890s or early 1920s by Frank Peer Beal
origin.editorNote: POP Tennis site (checked 2026-10-24) gives the USPTA history but not Beal or a founding date

governingBodyFact.text: International POP Tennis Association (formerly the United States Paddle Tennis Association)
governingBodyFact.editorNote: Corrected from "POP Tennis (formerly the United States Paddle Tennis Association)" on 2026-10-24. USPTA rebranded the sport POP Tennis in 2015 and renamed itself the International POP Tennis Association in late 2016; current activity not confirmed after 2018

name: Paddleball
summary: Paddleball is a wall game played with a solid paddle and a rubber ball, struck against a front wall in turn. There are four-wall versions played on racquetball courts and a one-wall version popular on the outdoor courts of New York City.

origin.text: Four-wall paddleball was developed around 1930 at the University of Michigan
origin.editorNote: National Paddleball Association site (paddleball.org) checked 2026-10-24: no history page. Earl Riskey, University of Michigan, around 1930 is commonly cited

governingBodyFact.editorNote: Site calls itself the official website of the National Paddleball Association (four-wall game); last updated around 2013, so current activity is unconfirmed

name: Frescobol
summary: Frescobol is a Brazilian beach game in which two players with wooden paddles keep a rubber ball in the air between them for as long as possible. It is co-operative rather than competitive: there is no net, no court and usually no winner.

origin.text: Created on Copacabana beach, Rio de Janeiro, in the 1940s
origin.editorNote: Commonly credited to Lian Pinto. Confirm. No official source found or checked in the 2026-10-24 verification pass.

governingBodyFact.editorNote: No single international governing body known; check for national associations. No official source found or checked in the 2026-10-24 verification pass.

name: Matkot
summary: Matkot is Israel's beach paddle game: two players hit a small rubber ball back and forth with wooden paddles, trying to keep the rally going. It is played on Israeli beaches and has a competitive form in which pairs are scored on the speed and length of their rallies.

origin.text: Popular on Tel Aviv beaches since around the 1930s
origin.editorNote: Origin dating varies. Confirm. No official source found or checked in the 2026-10-24 verification pass.

governingBodyFact.editorNote: Israeli Matkot association reported; confirm name. No official source found or checked in the 2026-10-24 verification pass.

name: Ball badminton
summary: Ball badminton is an Indian net sport played with light rackets and a yellow ball made of wool, on a larger court than badminton and in teams of five a side. It is fast and played mainly in southern India.

origin.text: Originated in Tanjore (Thanjavur), Tamil Nadu, India, where it drew the interest of the Maharaja of Tanjore
origin.editorNote: Corrected from "Played in India since at least the mid 19th century, associated with Tanjore (Thanjavur)" on 2026-10-24; the BBFI gives no date (1856 is commonly cited)

governingBodyFact.editorNote: Federation website loaded; no international federation found

relatedSports.relation: Shares the name, uses a ball

name: Jokari
summary: Jokari is a game in which a rubber ball tied by a long elastic cord to a heavy base is struck with wooden bats; it springs back after each hit, so one player can practise alone or two can take turns. It is played on beaches and in gardens, mainly in France.

origin.text: Associated with the French Basque country, early 20th century
origin.editorNote: Origin date and inventor uncertain. Confirm. No official source found or checked in the 2026-10-24 verification pass.

governingBodyFact.editorNote: No governing body known. No official source found or checked in the 2026-10-24 verification pass.

name: Frontenis
summary: Frontenis is a pelota discipline played on a three-walled fronton with tennis-style rackets and a hard rubber ball, struck against the front wall. It is one of the official disciplines of the International Federation of Basque Pelota and is especially popular in Mexico.

origin.text: Associated with Mexico, where the racquetball-ball form used at world championships began
origin.editorNote: Corrected from "Developed in Mexico in the early 20th century" on 2026-10-24; FIPV gives no date (around 1900 is commonly cited)

name: Paleta (Basque pelota)
summary: Paleta is a group of Basque pelota disciplines played with a solid wooden bat (the pala or paleta) against the front wall of a fronton or inside a trinquete. Versions use leather or rubber balls, and pala corta and paleta goma are among the FIPV's official disciplines.

origin.text: Paleta goma, the rubber-ball form, was born and developed in South America, where Argentina and Uruguay lead the sport
origin.editorNote: Corrected from "Grew out of the Basque handball game; paleta goma (rubber ball) is associated with Argentina" on 2026-10-24

name: Xare
summary: Xare is a Basque pelota discipline played in a trinquete, an enclosed indoor court, using a wooden hoop strung loosely with net (the xare) that catches and flings the ball. It is an FIPV discipline and is played mainly in the French Basque country and Argentina.

origin.text: Played in Argentina and the Basque country
origin.editorNote: FIPV xare page (checked 2026-10-24) says France dominates the speciality but gives no origin

name: Rackets
summary: Rackets is a fast, historic indoor game played with long wooden-framed rackets and a small, hard white ball in a large four-walled court with a high front wall. It survives mainly at British public schools, a few clubs, and in North America, and is the ancestor of squash.

origin.text: Grew out of games played against the yard walls of London's debtors' prisons, the King's Bench and the Fleet, in the 18th century
origin.editorNote: Corrected from "Grew out of games played against walls in London's debtors' prisons, notably the Fleet, in the 18th century" on 2026-10-24

relatedSports.relation: Same governing body in the UK

name: Squash 57
summary: Squash 57 is played on a squash court with a larger, bouncier ball and a shorter racket, which gives longer rallies and makes it easier to pick up than squash. It was known as racketball in Britain until England Squash renamed it, the name referring to the ball's 57 mm diameter.

origin.text: Developed in Britain in the 1970s as racketball; renamed Squash 57
origin.editorNote: WSF Squash 57 pages (checked 2026-10-24) confirm the former name racketball but give no date or place for the rename

governingBodyFact.editorNote: World Squash publishes the Squash 57 rules (worldsquash.sport/squash-57/squash-57-rules); England Squash's role not checked

name: AirBadminton
summary: AirBadminton is the outdoor form of badminton promoted by the Badminton World Federation, played on hard courts, grass or sand with a wind-resistant shuttle called the AirShuttle. Triples and doubles are the main formats.

origin.text: Launched by the BWF in 2019
origin.editorNote: BWF development site returned 403 on 2026-10-24. Badminton Oceania's 2020 guide gives no launch date; testing in 2019 and a global launch campaign in 2020 are reported

name: Squash tennis
summary: Squash tennis is an American wall game played on a squash-style court with a lively, inflated ball and tennis-like rackets. It was popular in New York clubs in the early 20th century and is now rarely played.

origin.text: Developed in New York in the late 19th century
origin.editorNote: Confirm. No official source found or checked in the 2026-10-24 verification pass.

governingBodyFact.editorNote: Historic National Squash Tennis Association; confirm current status. No official source found or checked in the 2026-10-24 verification pass.

name: Touchtennis
summary: Touchtennis is a short-court form of tennis played with 21-inch rackets and foam balls on a small court, which keeps the tactics of tennis while needing far less space. It is played mainly in the UK.

origin.text: Started in London in the 2000s
origin.editorNote: Begun in summer 2002 on the outskirts of London by Rashid Ahmad (not Michael Bennett, as previously noted)

governingBodyFact.editorNote: Organised by Touchtennis (UK). Confirm. No official source found or checked in the 2026-10-24 verification pass.

name: Spec tennis
summary: Spec tennis is a small-court game played with solid paddles and a low-compression tennis ball, using tennis scoring on a court the size of a pickleball court. It is played mainly in the United States.

origin.text: Created in Northern California in 2016 as a social game for pickleball courts
origin.editorNote: Corrected from "Developed in the United States in the 2000s" on 2026-10-24

governingBodyFact.editorNote: No US Spec Tennis Association found on spectennis.com (checked 2026-10-24)

name: Racketlon
summary: Racketlon is a combination event in which two players meet in four racket sports in turn — table tennis, badminton, squash and tennis — playing one set of each, with the winner decided on total points across all four.

origin.text: Developed in the Nordic countries (Finland and Sweden) in the 1980s-90s
origin.editorNote: FIR traces it to Finland in the mid-1980s (mailapelit; first Finnish Championships, Helsinki 1986) and Sweden from 1989

governingBodyFact.editorNote: FIR is a non-profit with its head office in Switzerland

name: Tamburello
summary: Tamburello is a traditional Italian team game in which players strike a rubber ball with a tambourine-like frame covered in a tight membrane. Teams face each other across a long open-air field, and the game is played mainly in northern Italy and parts of France.

origin.text: A traditional game from parts of Italy and France, developed mainly in Italy
origin.editorNote: Corrected from "Traditional game of northern Italy" on 2026-10-24

governingBodyFact.editorNote: Italian national federation; its site also links an international federation, not checked

name: Longue paume
summary: Longue paume is the historic French outdoor form of jeu de paume, played between teams on a long open field with light rackets and a small ball. It survives in northern France, notably in Paris and Picardy.

origin.text: Descended from the medieval French jeu de paume; rackets replaced the hand in the 16th century
origin.editorNote: Confirm. No official source found or checked in the 2026-10-24 verification pass.

governingBodyFact.editorNote: Confirm name. No official source found or checked in the 2026-10-24 verification pass.
